description: Between 1347 and 1353, the bubonic plague killed 30 to 60% of Europeans. A health catastrophe which shakes medieval society and accelerates the shift towards a new world.

hero.hook: In six years, Europe loses up to half of its population.

blocks.text: Between **1347** and **1353**, Europe is struck by the **Black Death**. Caused by the bacterium **Yersinia pestis**, it kills between **30 and 60%** of the population, or **25 to 50 million** people.

Europeans are already weakened by the famines of , a cooling of the climate which has spoiled the harvests. The scourge is not just a health crisis. It is a historical accelerator: it shakes the seigniorial order and forces society to rebuild itself differently. [[Little Ice Age]]

The bacteria first circulates among rodents in Central Asia. The [[Pax Mongolica]], a period of relative peace under the Mongol Empire, and the [[Silk Road]], a trade network linking Asia to Europe, offered him safe routes. At the Genoese counter of, in Crimea, besieged by the [[Caffa]] (a Mongol empire of the steppes), the disease shifts towards the Mediterranean. Galleys flee to Italy. [[Golden Horde]]

blocks.caption: Plague burials: Europe discovers mass death.

blocks.text: In **October 1347**, they docked at **Messina**, in Sicily. Despite the expulsion of the ships, evil is already at the dock. In **1348**, he reached Marseille, then all of Europe via the networks of Italian merchants.
The siege of Caffa is often cited as one of the first examples of biological warfare: the Mongols are said to have catapulted infected corpses over the walls.

Doctors rely on, an ancient Greek physician, and: the idea that diseases come from corrupted air. They do not see the real vector, the rat flea (). When the rats die [[Galen]], the fleas move on to humans. [[Miasma theory]] [[Xenopsylla cheopis]]

blocks.caption: The plague doctor with the beaked mask: a protection more symbolic than effective.

blocks.text: The bubonic form swells the lymph nodes. Sepsis turns the skin black. Pneumonia is transmitted from man to man and kills in **24 to 48 hours**. In crowded and dirty cities, the spread is very rapid.

Society is faltering. The [[Flagellants]] whip themselves in public to appease God. Art invents the Danses Macabres. In the absence of an explanation, we look for culprits: the [[Pogroms of Jews (1348-1349)]] are bloodying the Rhône valley and the Germanic Empire. Accused of poisoning the wells, thousands of Jews were massacred. Pope, then in Avignon, tried to protect them. Too little, too late. [[Clement VI]]
In Avignon, Clement VI remained between two large fires to “purify the air”. The heat kept the fleas at bay: he survived.
, a Florentine writer, describes fathers abandoning their sons. Charity, the neighborhood, the family: everything is crumbling under the fear of contagion. [[Boccaccio]]

blocks.text: Toward **1353**, the pandemic is ebbing. Labor has become scarce. Wages are rising, corvées are falling, serfdom is declining in the West. The lords must negotiate. The disaster has, paradoxically, strengthened the survivors.

The failure of the authorities in the face of the scourge also fuels critical thinking. We observe more, we doubt the old dogmas. By emptying villages and redistributing inheritances, the Black Death, despite itself, prepared the ground for the Renaissance.
Between **1347** and **1353**, the Black Death killed up to half of Europe. This demographic shock weakens the seigniorial order, raises the price of labor and accelerates entry into a new world.
